title: The tree climber
translation: There was a man people called the famous tree climber. He had someone climb a tall tree to cut the top branches. While it looked really dangerous, he said nothing. Only when the man was on his way down, at about the height of the roof, did he call up: "Careful now. Watch yourself on the way down."
"He could jump from there," I said. "Why tell him now?"
"That's the point," he said. "Up where it makes you dizzy and the branches might break, he's scared enough already, so I don't say anything. Mistakes always happen once you get to the easy part."

He was a common labourer, but that is exactly what the sages teach. The court football game, where you keep the ball in the air, is apparently the same: you get the ball out of a hard spot, think the rest is easy, and that's when you drop it.
original: {高名|かうみやう}の{木|き}のぼりといひし{男|をのこ}、{人|ひと}を{掟|おき}てて、{高|たか}き{木|き}にのぼせて{梢|こずゑ}をきらせしに、
いと{危|あやふ}く{見|み}えしほどはいふこともなくて、おるる{時|とき}に、{軒|のき}だけばかりになりて、「あやまちすな。{心|こころ}しておりよ。」と{言葉|ことば}をかけ{侍|はべ}りしを、
「かばかりになりては、{飛|と}び{降|お}るるともおりなむ。{如何|いか}にかくいふぞ。」と{申|まう}し{侍|はべ}りしかば、
「その{事|こと}に{候|さうらふ}。{目|め}くるめき{枝|えだ}{危|あやふ}きほどは、おのれがおそれ{侍|はべ}れば{申|まう}さず。
あやまちは{安|やす}き{所|ところ}になりて、{必|かなら}ず{仕|つかまつ}ることに{候|さうらふ}。」といふ。
あやしき{下臈|げらふ}なれども、{聖人|せいじん}のいましめにかなへり。
{鞠|まり}もかたき{所|ところ}を{蹴|け}{出|いだ}して{後|のち}、やすくおもへば、{必|かなら}ずおつと{侍|はべ}るやらむ。
literal: A man who was called the famous tree climber directed a person, had him climb a tall tree and cut the treetop;
while it looked very dangerous, he said nothing, (but) when (the man) was coming down and got to about the height of the eaves, he called out, 'Don't make a mistake. Come down carefully.'
When I said, 'Once he is this low, he could get down even if he jumped. Why do you say that?',
he said, 'That is just it. While it is dizzying and the branches are dangerous, he is afraid himself, so I say nothing.
Mistakes are always made when one gets to the easy places.'
He is a humble low-ranking man, but it accords with the warnings of the sages.
In kickball too, after you kick (the ball) out of a hard spot and think it easy, it surely falls, they say, I believe.

notes.text: {高名|かうみやう}: 'famous'. Tree climbers pruned and cut down tall trees in temple and noble gardens. This one is a master who no longer climbs himself but directs others.
{掟|おき}つ: 'to give orders, to direct'. The noun {掟|おきて} 'rule' (still used today) comes from it.
'About the height of the eaves': the edge of a single-storey roof, so a few metres up.
き (here しか): the past of something the writer experienced himself. Kenkō was there and asked the question. Compare けり in section 52, for stories he only heard.
{下臈|げらふ}: a person of low rank. あやし here means 'humble, lowly', not modern 'suspicious'.
Commentators usually point to the Classic of Changes, a Confucian classic: 'when you are safe, do not forget danger'.
{鞠|まり}: {蹴鞠|けまり}, a game played at court in which a group of players keep a deerskin ball in the air with their feet. Some noble families taught it as a hereditary art.

notes.quote: 必ずおつと侍るやらむ
notes.text: やらむ: 'I believe, it seems'. Kenkō passes this on as something he has heard, without claiming to know the game himself.
